item.title: Postgres SELECT DISTINCT scans every matching row despite indexes
item.description: In a Postgres-backed queue workload, SELECT DISTINCT became the most expensive query because it scans every row matching the predicates, even when few unique values are needed. The explanation of the database's design trade-offs and workarounds can inform high-volume query design.

item.title: Safe-not-safe checks Postgres migrations with a browser-based parser
item.description: The tool uses libpg_query 17 compiled to WebAssembly in a browser worker, with a rule engine and no telemetry. It may help teams catch risky migration patterns, though the excerpt does not describe the rules or their coverage.
